_doc: Zone guides of the western USA (Southwest, California, Northwest, Wild West, Colorado), written by hand with sources, 2026-11-17. Same rules as todo.json.

areas.season: Desert city: 40 °C in July and August, mild 15-25 °C from November to March, cool nights in winter.
areas.sleep: On the Strip, or downtown near Fremont Street for less.

items.name: The Strip at night
items.why: The Bellagio fountains every 15-30 minutes after dark, the Eiffel Tower of Paris Las Vegas and the neon of the old casinos on Fremont Street.

items.name: Red Rock Canyon scenic drive
items.book: Timed-entry reservation for the scenic drive from October to May (recreation.gov).
items.why: A 21 km one-way loop under red and cream sandstone cliffs 30 minutes from the Strip, with short walks to rock art and Calico Hills.

items.name: Valley of Fire
items.why: Nevada's oldest state park: red Aztec sandstone, the Fire Wave and 2,000-year-old petroglyphs on Atlatl Rock, an hour from town.

items.name: Hoover Dam
items.why: The 221 m concrete arch of 1936 across Black Canyon, from the top and from the bridge walkway beside it.

areas.season: Open all year. Spring and autumn are best; summer is hot (35 °C) with afternoon storms and flash floods in July-September; winter is quiet, with ice on the high trails.
areas.sleep: Springdale, at the park gate, on the shuttle line.

items.name: Angels Landing
items.best: Start early: the shuttle from 6-7 am.
items.book: Permit by lottery, seasonal and day-before (recreation.gov). Without it, Scout Lookout below the chains is open to all.
items.why: A narrow fin of sandstone 450 m above the canyon floor, the last stretch along chains with drops on both sides.

items.name: The Narrows from the bottom
items.book: No permit to Big Spring. Closed when the river flows over 150 cubic feet per second (often in spring melt) and on flash-flood warnings: check at the visitor centre.
items.why: Walking up the Virgin River between walls 300 m high and 6 m apart in places, in the water most of the way.

items.name: Emerald Pools
items.why: Pools and a thin waterfall under the cliffs of Zion Lodge, an easy first walk from the shuttle.

items.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
items.why: A short ledge path on the east side above the switchbacks, ending on a view down the whole of Zion Canyon; bighorn sheep around.

items.name: Riverside Walk and the canyon by shuttle
items.why: The flat paved walk to the mouth of the Narrows, after the shuttle ride under the Great White Throne.

areas.season: At 2,400-2,700 m: snow on the hoodoos December to March (rim open, some trails icy), cool summer nights, storms in July and August.
areas.sleep: Bryce Canyon City by the park gate, or the lodge inside.

items.name: Navajo Loop and Queens Garden
items.why: Down among the orange hoodoos through Wall Street's slot to Thor's Hammer and Queen Victoria's rock, back up to the rim.

items.name: Sunrise and the rim between Sunrise and Inspiration Point
items.why: The flat rim path above the whole amphitheatre of hoodoos, at its best at sunrise.

items.name: Fairyland Loop
items.why: The quieter north of the park: 13 km round hoodoos, Tower Bridge and the China Wall.

items.name: Night sky
items.why: One of the darkest skies in the country: the Milky Way over the rim, with ranger astronomy talks in summer.

areas.season: Hot summers (36 °C), cold clear winters; Antelope Canyon light beams are a summer midday thing (late March to early October).
areas.sleep: Page town.

items.name: Antelope Canyon
items.book: Navajo guided tours only (Upper or Lower), book ahead.
items.why: A slot canyon of wave-shaped red sandstone on Navajo land, lit by beams of sun at midday in summer.

items.name: Horseshoe Bend
items.why: A loop of the Colorado River 300 m below a sandstone rim, a short walk from the road.

items.name: Lake Powell by boat or kayak
items.why: A reservoir of 300 km in red canyons; kayak from Lone Rock or the Antelope Point marina into Antelope Canyon from the water.

areas.season: South Rim open all year at 2,100 m: snow and -5 °C nights in winter, 30 °C in summer; down in the canyon it is 15 °C hotter. North Rim only mid-May to mid-October.
areas.sleep: Grand Canyon Village lodges, or Tusayan outside the gate.

items.name: The Rim Trail and sunset at Hopi Point
items.why: The paved path along the edge from Mather Point, then the Hermit Road shuttle to Hopi Point for the sunset over a mile-deep canyon.

items.name: South Kaibab to Ooh Aah Point or Cedar Ridge
items.why: Down a ridge into the canyon instead of looking at it: Cedar Ridge is 460 m below the rim; the climb back takes twice as long.

items.name: Desert View Drive and Watchtower
items.why: 40 km east along the rim to the 1932 watchtower of Mary Colter, where the Colorado bends below the Painted Desert.

items.name: Bright Angel Trail to the 1.5-Mile Resthouse
items.why: The old mule path in switchbacks below the village, with water at the resthouses in season.

areas.season: High desert at 1,700 m: hot summer days, cold winter nights, the valley open all year.
areas.sleep: The View Hotel or Goulding's Lodge, the only beds for 40 km.

items.name: Valley Drive and a Navajo guide
items.book: Park fee; guided tours at the visitor centre.
items.why: The 27 km dirt loop between the Mittens and Merrick Butte, then with a Navajo guide into the parts closed to cars.

items.name: Wildcat Trail round the West Mitten
items.why: The only walk you may do without a guide: 5 km round the base of the West Mitten.

items.name: Forrest Gump Point at sunrise
items.why: The straight road of US-163 running into the buttes, where the film's run ended.

areas.season: Best March-May and September-October; 38 °C in July, snow on the arches some winter days. Arches needs a timed entry from April to October.
areas.sleep: Moab town, 10 minutes from Arches.

items.name: Delicate Arch
items.book: Arches timed-entry reservation April-October, 7 am-4 pm (recreation.gov).
items.why: Up bare slickrock to the free-standing arch on Utah's licence plates, the La Sal Mountains behind it.

items.name: Mesa Arch and Grand View Point
items.why: Canyonlands' Island in the Sky: the sun rising under Mesa Arch, then the view from Grand View Point over two rivers' canyons.

items.name: The Windows and Double Arch
items.why: Three great arches a short walk from one car park, the easiest of Arches.

items.name: Dead Horse Point at sunset
items.why: A mesa-top state park above a gooseneck of the Colorado 600 m below.

items.name: Fiery Furnace with a ranger
items.book: Ranger tour or self-guided permit (recreation.gov), sells out.
items.why: A maze of sandstone fins where you scramble and squeeze, on a ranger walk or with a permit.

areas.season: Quieter than the other Utah parks; spring and autumn best, orchards ripe June to October, snow some winter days.
areas.sleep: Torrey, 15 minutes west.

items.name: Hickman Bridge
items.why: A natural bridge of 40 m above a dry wash, reached on a short climb from the Fremont River.

items.name: Scenic Drive and Capitol Gorge
items.why: The road along the Waterpocket Fold's cliffs into a narrow gorge where pioneers carved their names in 1871.

items.name: Fruita orchards and petroglyphs
items.why: Mormon orchards where you pick fruit in season, a pie at the Gifford Homestead, and Fremont petroglyphs on the cliff.

items.name: Cassidy Arch
items.why: Up the side of Grand Wash to the arch named after Butch Cassidy, who hid nearby.

areas.season: Mild winters (14 °C, cold nights), hot summers (35 °C) with July-August storms; the red rocks at their best in spring and autumn.
areas.sleep: Sedona or the Village of Oak Creek.

items.name: Cathedral Rock
items.why: A short steep scramble up red slickrock to the saddle between Cathedral Rock's spires.

items.name: Chapel of the Holy Cross and Bell Rock
items.why: A chapel of 1956 built into the red rock, and the bell-shaped butte by the road south.

items.name: Oak Creek Canyon and Slide Rock
items.why: Up the green canyon north of town to swim and slide down a natural chute of sandstone.

items.name: Red rocks by jeep
items.why: Off-road tracks onto the rocks around town, where cars can't go.

areas.season: The hottest place on earth: 47 °C in July, walks only before 10 am from May to September. November to March is mild (20 °C) and best.
areas.sleep: Furnace Creek or Stovepipe Wells.

items.name: Zabriskie Point, Badwater and Artists Palette
items.why: Sunrise on the gold badlands of Zabriskie Point, then the salt flats of Badwater 86 m below the sea and the coloured hills of Artists Drive.

items.name: Golden Canyon
items.why: A walk up a yellow canyon to the Red Cathedral, the easiest way into the badlands.

items.name: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes
items.why: Dunes of 30 m by Stovepipe Wells, at sunset or under the stars.

items.name: Dante's View
items.why: 1,669 m above Badwater: the whole valley white below and Telescope Peak opposite.

areas.season: Best October to April (20-25 °C days, cold nights); 40 °C in summer, when walks are only for early morning.
areas.sleep: Twentynine Palms or Joshua Tree town, by the north gates.

items.name: Hidden Valley and the boulder piles
items.why: A loop through a valley ringed by granite boulders where cattle rustlers hid, among the Joshua trees.

items.name: Ryan Mountain
items.why: The park's best view for the effort: 320 m up to a summit over the boulder fields and the Joshua tree forest.

items.name: Cholla Cactus Garden and Keys View
items.why: A field of silver teddy-bear cholla at sunrise, and Keys View over the Coachella Valley to the San Andreas Fault.

items.name: Night sky
items.why: A dark-sky park: the Milky Way over the Joshua trees on moonless nights.

areas.season: Cool all year (14-22 °C), summer fog on the bay in June-August, the clearest days in September-October; rain November to March.
areas.sleep: Union Square, Nob Hill or North Beach, near the cable cars.

items.name: Golden Gate Bridge on foot
items.why: Across the 2.7 km bridge on its east walkway from the Presidio to Vista Point, the city and Alcatraz behind you.

items.name: Alcatraz
items.book: Sells out weeks ahead: only through Alcatraz City Cruises from Pier 33.
items.why: The ferry to the island prison of 1934-1963, with the cellhouse audio tour told by former guards and inmates.

items.name: Cable car, Chinatown and Lombard Street
items.why: The Powell-Hyde cable car over Nob Hill to the crooked block of Lombard Street, back through Chinatown and North Beach.

items.name: Fisherman's Wharf and the sea lions of Pier 39
items.why: Clam chowder in sourdough bread and the sea lions lying on the floats of Pier 39.

items.name: Muir Woods and Sausalito
items.book: Parking or shuttle reservation for Muir Woods (gomuirwoods.com).
items.why: Coast redwoods 70 m tall in a canyon over the bridge, then the ferry back from Sausalito's houseboats.

areas.season: Valley open all year: waterfalls fullest April-June, dry by August; snow in winter (chains may be required). Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road are closed about November to May.
areas.sleep: In the valley (lodges, Curry Village), or El Portal and Mariposa outside.

items.name: Mist Trail to Vernal Fall and Nevada Fall
items.why: Granite steps beside two waterfalls, in their spray in spring, to the top of 181 m Nevada Fall.

items.name: The valley floor: Yosemite Falls, El Capitan, Tunnel View
items.why: The lower Yosemite Fall, the climbers on El Capitan from the meadow, and Tunnel View, the picture of the valley with Half Dome.

items.name: Glacier Point
items.why: From 975 m above the valley, Half Dome face on and the Vernal and Nevada falls in one view.

items.name: Half Dome
items.book: Cables permit by preseason lottery in March and daily lottery (recreation.gov). Cables up about late May to mid-October.
items.why: The cables up the last 120 m of the granite dome, after 14 km of trail: the hike of Yosemite.

items.name: Mariposa Grove of giant sequoias
items.why: 500 giant sequoias at the south entrance, the Grizzly Giant among them, about 2,000 years old.

areas.season: Reached from Yosemite only over Tioga Pass (about June to October). Dry: hot summer days in the Owens Valley, cool at the lakes; snow and ski at Mammoth in winter.
areas.sleep: Bishop, or Lee Vining by Mono Lake.

items.name: Mono Lake's tufa towers
items.why: Limestone towers that grew under a salt lake, left on the shore when Los Angeles took its water.

items.name: Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest
items.why: Gnarled pines at 3,000 m in the White Mountains, some over 4,000 years old; Methuselah grows here unmarked.

items.name: Alabama Hills and Mount Whitney
items.why: Round orange boulders and Mobius Arch under the Sierra crest and Mount Whitney, the highest peak of the lower 48 (4,421 m).

items.name: Devils Postpile and Rainbow Falls
items.why: Columns of basalt like organ pipes, then a 30 m waterfall, by shuttle from Mammoth.

areas.season: Alpine lake at 1,900 m: summer 25 °C and cold water; ski December to April (Heavenly, Palisades); snow on the roads in winter.
areas.sleep: South Lake Tahoe, or Tahoe City on the north shore.

items.name: Emerald Bay and Vikingsholm
items.why: Down to the 1929 Scandinavian castle on the bay, and along the Rubicon Trail above the clearest water of the lake.

items.name: Sand Harbor
items.why: Granite boulders in turquoise water on the Nevada shore; kayak or swim if you can take 18 °C.

items.name: Skiing at Heavenly or Palisades
items.why: Big Sierra resorts above the lake, Heavenly's runs crossing from California into Nevada.

areas.season: Mild; harvest and crush in September-October, green hills in winter rain, hot dry summer days.
areas.sleep: Napa, Yountville or Healdsburg.

items.name: Wineries of Napa and Sonoma
items.book: Most tastings by reservation.
items.why: Cabernet in the valley that beat France at the 1976 Judgment of Paris, tasting room by tasting room.

items.name: Calistoga mud baths
items.why: Volcanic ash and hot spring water at the top of the valley.

areas.season: Cool coast all year (15-20 °C), summer fog; Highway 1 through Big Sur is sometimes cut by landslides: check Caltrans.
areas.sleep: Monterey or Carmel.

items.name: Big Sur by Highway 1
items.why: South along the cliffs to Bixby Bridge, Pfeiffer Beach and McWay Falls dropping onto a cove beach.

items.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium and Cannery Row
items.why: A kelp forest three floors high and sea otters, in the old sardine cannery of Steinbeck's novel.

items.name: Point Lobos
items.why: Cypress headlands, sea otters and harbour seals in the coves, 'the greatest meeting of land and water in the world'.

items.name: 17-Mile Drive and Carmel
items.why: The Lone Cypress on its rock, Pebble Beach's links, then the cottages of Carmel-by-the-Sea.

areas.season: Mediterranean climate: 18-25 °C, sunny most of the year, rain in winter.
areas.sleep: Downtown or by the beach.

items.name: Mission and old town
items.why: The 'Queen of the Missions' of 1786 and the white Spanish-revival town rebuilt after the 1925 earthquake, to Stearns Wharf.

items.name: Channel Islands by boat
items.book: Island Packers boats from Ventura, book ahead.
items.why: The ferry from Ventura to Santa Cruz Island: sea caves by kayak, island foxes, dolphins on the crossing.

items.name: Funk Zone wine tasting
items.why: Tasting rooms in old warehouses by the beach.

areas.season: Sunny all year: 20 °C in winter, 30 °C in summer inland, June gloom on the coast in June; rain only a few winter days.
areas.sleep: Santa Monica by the sea, or Hollywood.

items.name: Griffith Observatory and the Hollywood Sign
items.why: Up Mount Hollywood's paths to the art-deco observatory, the Hollywood Sign and the city to the sea.

items.name: Santa Monica Pier and Venice
items.why: The end of Route 66 on the pier, then the boardwalk to Venice's skaters and canals.

items.name: Hollywood Boulevard
items.why: The stars of the Walk of Fame and the hand prints of the Chinese Theatre.

items.name: The Getty Center
items.book: Free timed ticket; parking fee.
items.why: A hilltop of white travertine with Van Gogh's Irises and gardens over the city; free entry.

items.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
items.book: Tickets online.
items.why: The studio tour through the back lots, and the rides.

areas.season: The mildest climate of the US: 20 °C in winter, 25 °C in summer.
areas.sleep: Gaslamp Quarter, Little Italy or La Jolla.

items.name: La Jolla Cove and Torrey Pines
items.why: Sea lions on the rocks of the cove, then the bluffs of Torrey Pines over the Pacific.

items.name: Balboa Park and the zoo
items.why: Spanish-revival palaces of 1915 with museums, and the San Diego Zoo beside them.

items.name: USS Midway and the harbour
items.why: An aircraft carrier of 1945 to walk through, by the tall ships of the Embarcadero.

items.name: Coronado Beach
items.why: Wide white sand in front of the Hotel del Coronado of 1888.

areas.season: The groves at 2,000 m: snow December to April (chains may be required, some roads closed), warm summer days; the foothills at Three Rivers are hot in summer.
areas.sleep: Three Rivers at the gate, or the lodges in the park.

items.name: General Sherman and the Congress Trail
items.why: The largest tree on earth by volume, then a loop through the groves of the Giant Forest.

items.name: Moro Rock
items.why: 400 steps up a granite dome to the Great Western Divide.

items.name: General Grant Tree, Kings Canyon
items.why: The nation's Christmas tree in Grant Grove, then the road down into Kings Canyon in summer.

areas.season: Cool and damp all year (10-20 °C), fog in summer, heavy rain in winter.
areas.sleep: Orick, Klamath or Crescent City.

items.name: Lady Bird Johnson Grove and Prairie Creek
items.why: Coast redwoods over 100 m, the tallest trees on earth, and Roosevelt elk grazing at Elk Prairie.

items.name: Fern Canyon
items.book: Parking permit May 15 to September 15 (recreation.gov).
items.why: A gully with walls of ferns 15 m high, reached over a gravel road on the beach.

items.name: Avenue of the Giants
items.why: 50 km of old road through Humboldt Redwoods south of the park.

areas.season: Dry sunny summers (July-September, 25 °C), grey and drizzly October to May but rarely cold.
areas.sleep: Downtown or Belltown, near Pike Place.

items.name: Pike Place Market and the waterfront
items.why: The 1907 market over Elliott Bay: fish stalls, the gum wall in Post Alley, then down to the piers.

items.name: Space Needle and Kerry Park
items.why: The 1962 World's Fair tower, then Kerry Park for the skyline with Mount Rainier behind it on a clear day.

items.name: Ferry to Bainbridge Island
items.why: 35 minutes across Puget Sound on the state ferry, the city skyline and the Olympics on either side.

areas.season: Paradise has snow from November to June (one of the snowiest measured places on earth); wildflower meadows late July to August; the Sunrise road only July to September.
areas.sleep: Ashford by the Nisqually entrance, or the Paradise Inn (May-October).

items.name: Skyline Trail at Paradise
items.why: Up through wildflower meadows to Panorama Point under the Nisqually Glacier, 4,392 m of volcano in front of you.

items.name: Snowshoeing at Paradise
items.book: Carry chains; the road to Paradise closes at night in winter.
items.why: Ranger snowshoe walks from the Paradise visitor centre in winter, when the meadows lie under metres of snow.

items.name: Reflection Lakes and Narada Falls
items.why: The mountain upside down in the water, and a 50 m fall by the road.

items.name: Grove of the Patriarchs and old-growth forest
items.why: Douglas firs and red cedars about 1,000 years old on an island in the Ohanapecosh River.

areas.season: Dry summers, very wet winters; Hurricane Ridge road has snow and limited winter access.
areas.sleep: Port Angeles, or the lodges at Lake Crescent and Sol Duc (spring to autumn).

items.name: Hurricane Ridge and Hurricane Hill
items.why: A road to 1,600 m, then the walk up Hurricane Hill over the snowfields of Mount Olympus and the Strait to Canada.

items.name: Lake Crescent and Marymere Falls
items.why: A deep glacial lake of blue water under forested mountains, and a forest path to a 27 m waterfall.

items.name: Sol Duc Falls and hot springs
items.why: A walk through old-growth forest to the fall splitting into three, then the hot pools.

areas.season: Over 3.5 m of rain a year, most from October to April; mild all year.
areas.sleep: Forks, or the Kalaloch Lodge on the coast.

items.name: Hall of Mosses
items.why: Maples and spruces hung with moss in one of the few temperate rainforests of the world.

items.name: Rialto Beach and Hole-in-the-Wall
items.book: Check the tide table: Hole-in-the-Wall only at low tide.
items.why: Driftwood logs and sea stacks on the wild Pacific coast, walking at low tide to a rock arch.

items.name: Ruby Beach and Kalaloch
items.why: Sea stacks off a beach of red-tinged pebbles, and the Tree of Life clinging over a void at Kalaloch.

areas.season: Mild: dry warm summers, grey drizzly winters.
areas.sleep: Downtown or the Pearl District.

items.name: Downtown, Powell's and food carts
items.why: Powell's City of Books, a whole city block of books, and lunch at the food-cart pods.

items.name: Japanese Garden and Washington Park
items.why: Maples, ponds and Mount Hood beyond the city from the hills of Washington Park.

areas.season: Windy (kitesurfing in summer at Hood River); the falls fullest in winter and spring; ice storms some winter days.
areas.sleep: Hood River.

items.name: Multnomah Falls and the waterfall corridor
items.book: Timed-use permit for the Historic Columbia River Highway corridor in summer (recreation.gov).
items.why: Oregon's 189 m waterfall in two drops under a stone bridge, then Latourell and Horsetail falls on the old highway.

items.name: Vista House and Crown Point
items.why: A 1918 stone rotunda 230 m above the river, looking up the whole gorge.

items.name: Hood River fruit loop and Mount Hood
items.why: Orchards and cider below Mount Hood's snow cone; windsurfers on the river.

areas.season: At 2,100 m with about 11 m of snow a year: the Rim Drive and north entrance open only about July to October; in winter only Rim Village, on snowshoes.
areas.sleep: Crater Lake Lodge or Mazama Village (summer), or outside the park.

items.name: Rim Drive
items.why: 53 km round the deepest lake of the US (594 m), blue from the caldera's clean water, with Wizard Island in it.

items.name: Cleetwood Cove down to the water
items.why: The only path to the shore, 210 m down; swim if you can take 15 °C.

items.name: Watchman Peak at sunset
items.why: A short climb to a fire lookout over Wizard Island.

areas.season: High desert, 300 sunny days a year: hot dry summers, snow and ski at Mount Bachelor November to May.
areas.sleep: Bend, on the Deschutes River.

items.name: Smith Rock
items.why: Volcanic tuff walls over a river bend, the birthplace of American sport climbing; the Misery Ridge trail climbs over it.

items.name: Newberry Volcano and the lava tubes
items.why: The obsidian flow and Lava River Cave, a 1.6 km lava tube, south of town.

items.name: Skiing at Mount Bachelor
items.why: A volcano skied from its summit in all directions, dry snow, a long season.

items.name: Deschutes River and the Old Mill
items.why: Float or walk the river through town past the old mill smokestacks.

areas.season: Summer days 25 °C, frost at night; the park roads open May to October (Moose-Wilson and Jenny Lake area); winter -15 °C with deep powder at Jackson Hole Mountain Resort.
areas.sleep: Jackson town, or Teton Village under the ski area.

items.name: Jenny Lake, Inspiration Point and Cascade Canyon
items.why: The shuttle boat across Jenny Lake, up past Hidden Falls to Inspiration Point and into Cascade Canyon under the Grand Teton; moose in the willows.

items.name: Mormon Row and Oxbow Bend at sunrise
items.why: The pioneer barns of 1910 under the Tetons, then the Snake River's Oxbow Bend with the mountain in the water.

items.name: Taggart Lake
items.why: An easy loop to a lake right under the Grand Teton, through a forest that burned in 1985.

items.name: Skiing Jackson Hole
items.why: Steep powder and the aerial tram to the top of Rendezvous Mountain.

items.name: Sleigh ride among the elk
items.why: Horse-drawn sleighs through some 7,000 elk wintering on the National Elk Refuge by the town.

items.name: Jackson town square
items.why: The arches of elk antlers on the square, cowboy bars and galleries.

areas.season: Roads open to cars about late April to early November; at 2,300 m, frost possible any night; in winter only snowcoaches and snowmobiles reach Old Faithful (mid-December to mid-March).
areas.sleep: Old Faithful Inn or Canyon Lodge inside (book a year ahead), or West Yellowstone.

items.name: Old Faithful and the Upper Geyser Basin
items.why: Old Faithful erupting about every 90 minutes, then the boardwalks past hundreds of geysers to Morning Glory Pool.

items.name: Grand Prismatic from the Fairy Falls overlook
items.why: The largest hot spring of the US seen from above, rings of orange and blue, then on to 61 m Fairy Falls.

items.name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone
items.why: Yellow walls and the 94 m Lower Falls from Artist Point and the brink of the falls.

items.name: Hayden Valley wildlife
items.why: Bison herds by the road, elk, and with luck a grizzly, at dawn or dusk.

items.name: Snowcoach to Old Faithful in winter
items.book: Snowcoach tours from West Yellowstone or Mammoth, mid-December to mid-March.
items.why: Over the snow-covered roads to the geysers steaming in -20 °C, bison frosted white.

areas.season: The North Entrance road to Mammoth and Lamar Valley is the only Yellowstone road open to cars all year; cold, snowy winters at 1,600-2,000 m.
areas.sleep: Gardiner, at the Roosevelt Arch.

items.name: Mammoth Hot Springs terraces
items.why: White travertine terraces built by hot water, on boardwalks over them.

items.name: Wolves in Lamar Valley
items.why: Before dawn in the 'Serengeti of North America', with the spotting scopes of wolf watchers along the road; bison and pronghorn all day.

items.name: Boiling River and Gardiner
items.why: Rafting the Yellowstone River in summer through Gardiner's canyon.

areas.season: Dry, sunny; summer rodeo every night June to August; the East Entrance road to Yellowstone open May to early November.
areas.sleep: Cody town.

items.name: Buffalo Bill Center of the West
items.why: Five museums in one: the West's art, Plains Indians, firearms and Yellowstone's natural history.

items.name: Cody Nite Rodeo
items.why: Bronc and bull riding every summer night in the 'Rodeo Capital of the World'.

areas.season: Going-to-the-Sun Road is fully open only about July to mid-October; snow on the passes into June; grizzly country (carry bear spray).
areas.sleep: West Glacier, Apgar or Whitefish; Many Glacier and St. Mary on the east side in summer.

items.name: Going-to-the-Sun Road and Logan Pass
items.book: Vehicle reservation for the road in summer (recreation.gov), or the park shuttle.
items.why: 80 km over the Continental Divide past waterfalls on the cliffs, with mountain goats at Logan Pass and the Hidden Lake overlook.

items.name: Highline Trail
items.why: From Logan Pass along a ledge on the Garden Wall to Granite Park Chalet, 18 km of the park's best views; out by the Loop.

items.name: Lake McDonald and Avalanche Lake
items.why: Coloured stones under clear water at Apgar, then the Trail of the Cedars to a lake under waterfalls.

items.name: Grinnell Glacier from Many Glacier
items.why: Past turquoise lakes to the glacier and its iceberg lake under the Garden Wall; grizzlies often seen on the slopes.

areas.season: University town at 1,460 m: warm dry summers, snowy winters with skiing at Big Sky December to April.
areas.sleep: Downtown Bozeman, or Big Sky for skiing.

items.name: Museum of the Rockies
items.why: One of the largest dinosaur collections in the world, with a full T. rex found in Montana.

items.name: Skiing at Big Sky
items.why: Lone Peak's tram to 3,403 m and one of the largest ski areas of the US.

items.name: Hyalite Canyon
items.why: Lakes and waterfalls in a canyon south of town; ice climbing in winter.

areas.season: Hot summers, cold winters with snow; Needles Highway closed in winter; Badlands and Rushmore open all year.
areas.sleep: Rapid City, Keystone or Custer.

items.name: Mount Rushmore and Crazy Horse
items.why: The four presidents carved into granite, and the unfinished mountain carving of Crazy Horse nearby.

items.name: Badlands National Park
items.why: Striped buttes and pinnacles of eroded clay on the prairie, the Door and Notch trails into them, bighorn and bison.

items.name: Custer State Park and Needles Highway
items.why: Granite needles and a tunnel road, Sylvan Lake, and bison herds on the Wildlife Loop.

items.name: Deadwood
items.why: The gold-rush town where Wild Bill Hickok was shot at the poker table in 1876.

areas.season: The Mile High City: 300 sunny days, warm summers, short snowfalls in winter that melt in days.
areas.sleep: LoDo, near Union Station.

items.name: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
items.why: A concert venue between two 90 m sandstone monoliths, and the trails round it in the foothills.

items.name: Union Station, LoDo and the Capitol
items.why: The restored 1914 station, brewpubs of Lower Downtown, and the gold-domed Capitol's step exactly a mile high.

areas.season: Trail Ridge Road (to 3,713 m) open about late May to mid-October; timed entry May to October; snowshoes at Bear Lake in winter.
areas.sleep: Estes Park.

items.name: Bear Lake to Dream and Emerald Lakes
items.book: Timed-entry reservation May-October (Bear Lake Road corridor), recreation.gov.
items.why: Three lakes in a row under Hallett Peak, 5 km from Bear Lake; snowshoes in winter.

items.name: Trail Ridge Road
items.why: The highest paved through-road of the US over the tundra at 3,700 m, elk and marmots by the road.

items.name: Sky Pond
items.why: Past Alberta Falls and The Loch, a scramble up beside Timberline Falls to a lake under the spires.

items.name: The elk rut in Moraine Park
items.why: Bull elk bugling and fighting in the meadows at dusk, mid-September to mid-October.

areas.season: Hot springs all year; Maroon Bells road to the lake mid-May to October (shuttle); skiing at Aspen and Vail December to April.
areas.sleep: Glenwood Springs, or Aspen (pricier).

items.name: Maroon Bells and Crater Lake
items.book: Shuttle or parking reservation from Aspen (aspenchamber.org).
items.why: The most photographed peaks of Colorado over Maroon Lake, then 3 km up to Crater Lake under their walls.

items.name: Hanging Lake
items.book: Permit required all year (visitglenwood.com).
items.why: A steep climb up a side canyon to a turquoise lake fed by thin waterfalls over a travertine rim.

items.name: Glenwood Hot Springs Pool
items.why: A two-block pool of spring water at 32-40 °C under red cliffs, open since 1888.

items.name: Skiing Aspen or Vail
items.why: Aspen's four mountains or Vail's back bowls, an hour from the springs.

areas.season: Warm dry summers; Mesa Verde cliff dwelling tours about May to October; the Silverton train runs to Silverton May to October, to Cascade Canyon in winter.
areas.sleep: Durango.

items.name: Mesa Verde cliff dwellings
items.book: Ranger tour tickets (recreation.gov).
items.why: Ancestral Puebloan villages of the 1200s built into cliff alcoves; ladders and tunnels on the ranger tours of Cliff Palace and Balcony House.

items.name: Durango & Silverton narrow-gauge railroad
items.book: Book ahead.
items.why: A coal steam train of 1882 along the Animas River gorge to the mining town of Silverton.

items.name: Skiing Purgatory
items.why: Family ski area 40 km north of town.

items.name: Million Dollar Highway to Ouray
items.why: Over Red Mountain Pass on a road without guardrails, to Ouray's hot springs.

areas.season: Sunny, dry; Pikes Peak summit (4,302 m) cold and windy, snow possible any month.
areas.sleep: Colorado Springs or Manitou Springs.

items.name: Garden of the Gods
items.why: Red sandstone fins tilted upright against Pikes Peak, free paths among them.

items.name: Pikes Peak by cog railway
items.book: Book the cog railway or the summit-road timed entry.
items.why: The highest cog railway in the world to 4,302 m, where 'America the Beautiful' was written.
